title: Fix 'Argument list too long' when a wildcard matches too many files
summary: The shell expands a wildcard such as * into a list of file names, and that list is too big for one command. Run the command through find and xargs instead, which splits the files into smaller batches.

aliases.text: bash argument list too long linux
ls * too many files in folder
слишком много файлов для команды linux
команда со звездочкой не работает много файлов
argument list too long что делать

prerequisites: Know the folder that contains the files
Know the command you wanted to run on them

steps.explain: Check the system limit on the total size of the arguments in one command. This is read-only. A typical value is about 2 MB.
steps.expect: A number such as 2097152 (about 2 MB). It is the maximum number of bytes for one command, including all file names.

steps.explain: Count the files in the folder. This is read-only. If the count is large, a wildcard such as * matches too many names for one command.

placeholders.name: DIR
placeholders.description: The folder with the files, without a trailing slash

steps.expect: A number of files. A count of tens of thousands or more with long names can exceed the limit.

steps.explain: Run your command on the files in small batches. find lists the matching files and xargs passes them to the command in pieces, so the limit is never exceeded. Replace ls -l with the command you wanted to run. Keep the pattern in single quotes.

placeholders.name: DIR
placeholders.description: The folder with the files, without a trailing slash

placeholders.name: PATTERN
placeholders.description: The file name pattern you used with the wildcard, in quotes

alternatives.explain: Same batching without a pipe: find passes the names to the command itself in batches.

placeholders.name: DIR
placeholders.description: The folder with the files, without a trailing slash

placeholders.name: PATTERN
placeholders.description: The file name pattern you used with the wildcard, in quotes

alternatives.expect: The same listing as the main command.

alternatives.explain: A loop handles one file at a time, so no command gets a long list. It is slow for many files, so use it for smaller folders.
alternatives.cmd: for f in <DIR>/<PATTERN>; do ls -l "$f"; done

placeholders.name: DIR
placeholders.description: The folder with the files, without a trailing slash

placeholders.name: PATTERN
placeholders.description: The file name pattern, for example *.jpg

alternatives.expect: One line per file, in the same order as the wildcard.

steps.expect: One line per matching file. The error does not appear.

warnings: Put the pattern in single quotes inside find, so the shell does not expand it before find runs.
Check the list first with the ls version. Do not replace ls -l with rm until the list is what you expect, because deleted files cannot be restored.
find -maxdepth 1 looks only at the folder itself, not at its subfolders.
